representation: For the SAME actual one-b endpoint matrix W of a hypothetical finite UD completion, J_i is the set of tails in head row i and C_l the set of heads in tail column l. For a fixed pair (i,l), all actual two-atom paths from first head i to last tail l have seam j+k with j in J_i and k in C_l.
finding: Actual-boundary a^n padding and UD imply J_i+C_l is direct for EVERY pair (i,l), so |J_i||C_l|<=n. Equivalently, for every seam s and fixed endpoints i,l, the sum over j+k=s of W[i,j]W[k,l] is at most 1. This is an all-variable length-two condition, not a claim that an arbitrary W satisfying it extends to a full code.
aggregate: If |W|=n, summing |J_i||C_l| over all i,l gives n². If R and C are maximum row and column sizes and h,t the numbers of nonempty rows and columns, then RC<=n, hR>=n, tC>=n, hence ht>=n. This latter conclusion is already immediate from a binary n-entry matrix and is not additional progress toward the original problem.
blocker: The direct packing condition is stronger than separate old-anchor row/column bounds, but its scalar aggregation gives no new exclusion. The first missing step is to exploit the pattern of overlaps among ALL pair-sum supports J_i+C_l together with the same endpoint matrix and arbitrary-length UD. Replacing that dependency by independently chosen marginals would be unsound.
status: WRITTEN at named actual-word scope, no formal or independent-family review. This is a representation/obstruction checkpoint, not a solved Shor completion problem; no held cofactor/fibre body was used.
